title: What can you say about vitamin E in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 1 wording for vitamin E; the strongest is "Helps protect cells from oxidative stress" (strong, 1.8-1,000 mg AT a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Prevents heart disease or cancer, outside FDA's qualified wording".

supported_wordings.wording: Helps protect cells from oxidative stress.
supported_wordings.why: Listed by Health Canada and authorized in the EU after EFSA review.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 19 and older. Health Canada: 1.0 mg AT up to 500 mg AT a day as dl-alpha-tocopherol, or up to 1,000 mg AT as d-alpha-tocopherol. EU: at least 1.8 mg, 15% of the 12 mg EU reference value (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex XIII).
supported_wordings.form: Alpha-tocopherol (d- or dl-) or its esters, counted as mg alpha-tocopherol (AT)

sources.name: Commission Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, list of permitted health claims

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Prevents heart disease or cancer, outside FDA's qualified wording
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names diseases. FDA's qualified claims on antioxidant vitamins and cancer have set wording (see fda_health_claims).

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

sources.name: Commission Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, list of permitted health claims
FDA qualified health claim: Antioxidant vitamins and risk of certain cancers
FDA qualified health claim: Vitamins C and E and site-specific cancers

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
